summary: Maestro2.11.0 waits for simctl openurl process completion and ordinary visual settling, not receipt by the app URL delegate. No supported synchronous app-delivery parameter was found in the pinned iOS path.

React Native0.81.5 native URL forwarding posts a synchronous notification, then emits through a queued callable-JS/runtime-scheduler path. This source structure is not a measurement of the cause or size of the observed delay.

Expo54.0.37 template forwards through super then RCTLinkingManager with short-circuit OR. Its generated b5 AppDelegate bytes were not retained; the new helper will retain the actual generated before/after bytes.

interpretationForNextRun: Early matched native entry/exit followed by late JS receipt would bound delay after the handler; it would not alone identify the RN scheduler or a specific cause.

Late matched native entry close to JS receipt would bound the delay before/at handler arrival, including OS/scene scheduling or app-main-thread availability; it would not prove OS or Maestro causality.
Entry without exit distinguishes an incomplete observed handler span, subject to log collection/termination limits.
Missing native markers do not by themselves prove no URL arrival: scope, count limit, build/source binding and log collection must be checked.
